summary: Current TS baseline is ../src/tools/SendMessageTool/SendMessageTool.ts plus registration in ../src/tools.ts. Per tools/reports/SendMessage.md, the removed bridge/Remote Control delivery path is treated as out of scope for Go parity; this report therefore focuses on teammate mailbox, local agent continuation, UDS, and structured control messages. The Go implementation has useful coverage for those paths, including mailbox writes, UDS, local-agent resume, request-id generation, and shutdown approval cancellation. Remaining parity gaps are concentrated in sender identity spoofing, loose input/schema and lifecycle metadata, Go-only MessageBus fallback/output, mailbox state/layout/read semantics, broadcast behavior, structured control payload/lifecycle details, permission/read-only handling, and stale alignment tests that assert non-current TS envelope behavior. Verification note: attempted `go test ./tools ./swarm ./permissions -run 'TestSendMessage|TestRequiresBridgePermission|TestIsMailboxRetryable|TestModeAllowAllSendMessage|TestCacheKeyDifferentiatesSendMessageTargets' -count=1`; `./swarm` had no matching tests and passed, while `./tools` and `./permissions` could not build because provider/responses.go references undefined classifyResponsesAPIError.

gaps.title: Go lets tool input spoof sender identity and authority
gaps.description: TS SendMessage input only accepts to, summary, and message; sender identity is derived from runtime/team state. Go's SendMessageInput adds from and content, then trusts from for mailbox sender selection, MessageBus reply routing, and structured plan-approval authority checks. A model/tool caller can therefore claim to be team-lead or another teammate in Go in ways the TS tool contract does not permit.

ts_evidence.note: TS input schema contains only to, optional summary, and message.
Plain mailbox sender is derived from getAgentName(), isTeammate(), and TEAM_LEAD_NAME, not from input.
Plan approval/rejection authority is checked against appState.teamContext via isTeamLead, and the payload is built from leader runtime state.

go_evidence.note: Go SendMessageInput includes Content and From fields that do not exist in the TS schema.
currentMessageSenderName returns in.From before env/team-derived senders.
MessageBus fallback uses input from, defaulting to user only when from is empty.
Plan approval response accepts senderName == team-lead, but senderName can originate from in.From.
Current tests exercise from as an input to drain pending replies, confirming this Go-only surface is active.

gaps.impact: A TS-invalid Go call can forge sender metadata, route/drain replies for another sender, and potentially pass leader-only structured-message checks by setting from=team-lead.

gaps.title: Go model-visible schema, description, availability, and read-only metadata are looser than TS
gaps.description: TS publishes a specific tool description, prompt, zod union for three structured message types, summary requirement for plain text except UDS, shouldDefer/searchHint, isEnabled via agent-swarms, and isReadOnly for string messages. Go publishes a broad object message schema, omits UDS/bridge from the visible to description despite supporting uds routing, exposes content/from as typed inputs, registers SendMessage unconditionally, and has no SendMessage-specific read-only hook in the tool interface.

ts_evidence.note: TS description is 'Send a message to another agent' and the prompt documents teammate, broadcast, UDS, bridge, and legacy protocol responses.
TS message schema is string or a discriminated union of shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response.
TS buildTool declares name/searchHint/maxResultSizeChars/shouldDefer, isEnabled(), and isReadOnly(input) for string messages.
TS base tools include SendMessage but TeamCreate/TeamDelete are gated by isAgentSwarmsEnabled; SendMessage availability is filtered by its own isEnabled() in normal getTools flow.

go_evidence.note: Go description says 'Send a message to a teammate agent'; schema allows message as any object and describes to only as teammate or broadcast.
Go typed input includes content/from fields absent from the model-visible TS schema.
SetupRegistry always registers SendMessage, while only TeamCreate/TeamDelete are gated by isAgentSwarmsEnabled.
Go has deferred-tool search metadata for SendMessage, but the search hint does not exactly match TS.
Core Go Tool interface has Name, Description, Schema, Execute only; there is no per-tool isReadOnly equivalent.

gaps.impact: The model is asked to call a different contract, Go accepts inputs TS would reject, UDS support is under-documented in the schema, SendMessage may be exposed in sessions where TS hides it, and permission/read-only behavior cannot match TS exactly.

gaps.title: Go falls back to a coordinator MessageBus/envelope path that TS SendMessage does not expose
gaps.description: For plain non-UDS messages, TS routes to local-agent continuation first and then mailbox write/broadcast. If no explicit teamName is available for a direct message, writeToMailbox defaults to the default team inbox. Go only uses mailbox routing when loadActiveTeamConfig returns a config; otherwise it routes through coordinator.MessageBus and returns an Envelope with request_id/kind/delivered/recipients/reply_text/quorum. Existing Go tests pin this Go-only path using content/from inputs.

ts_evidence.note: TS tries local-agent routing for string messages, then calls handleBroadcast for '*' or handleMessage for direct recipients.
handleMessage writes to the teammate mailbox and returns {success,message,routing}.
Mailbox path defaults to getTeamName() or 'default' when no teamName argument is supplied.
TS model-facing result is jsonStringify(data) from the SendMessage output union, not a MessageBus envelope.

go_evidence.note: Go mailbox routing only runs when loadActiveTeamConfig returns a config.
With no active team config, Go uses coordinator.MessageBus and returns an Envelope-shaped JSON response.
Envelope fields are request_id, kind, reply_to, delivered, recipients, reply_text, quorum, priority, and message.
Tests cover SendMessage delivery/failure through MessageBus using content rather than TS message+summary.
Tests also cover draining pending MessageBus replies via input from.

gaps.impact: A TS-compatible direct message can become a Go-only bus send, fail because the recipient is not subscribed, and return a non-TS envelope shape. This also makes tests green for behavior that is not in the current TS SendMessage baseline.

gaps.title: Mailbox file layout, read lifecycle, and routing metadata are not TS-compatible
gaps.description: TS mailbox messages are stored under a team-level inboxes directory, include a read boolean, preserve messages while marking them read, and SendMessage routing returns senderColor/targetColor when available. Go stores each recipient under {team}/{agent}/inbox.json, has no read field, reads by removing/clearing the inbox file, and SendMessage writes do not populate Color or return senderColor/targetColor even though TeamMember has a Color field.

ts_evidence.note: TS documents inbox files at .claude/teams/{team_name}/inboxes/{agent_name}.json.
TS TeammateMessage includes from, text, timestamp, read, optional color, and optional summary.
writeToMailbox appends a new message with read:false.
markMessagesAsRead updates read flags in-place rather than deleting the inbox file.
TS can find teammate colors from appState.teamContext.
Direct SendMessage routing includes senderColor and targetColor when available.

go_evidence.note: Go Message lacks a read field and documents inbox path as ~/.deepseek-code/teams/{teamName}/{agentName}/inbox.json.
Go inboxPath places each recipient under its own directory, not a shared inboxes directory.
Go Read reads and clears/removes the inbox file.
Go TeamMember has Color, but SendMessage does not use it.
Broadcast mailbox writes set From/Text/Summary only; no Color.
Direct mailbox writes and routing response omit Color, senderColor, and targetColor.

gaps.impact: Go mailboxes are not interchangeable with TS mailboxes, read state cannot be rendered or audited the same way, and UI/routing metadata loses teammate colors.

gaps.title: Broadcast validation, recipient selection, failure semantics, and output differ
gaps.description: TS broadcast requires an active team context and team file, broadcasts to every team file member except the sender regardless of isActive, and returns success true with message 'Message broadcast to N teammate(s): ...'. Go falls back to MessageBus broadcast when no team config is loaded, filters inactive persisted members, returns delivered/failed bookkeeping for mailbox broadcast, and uses a different message format.

ts_evidence.note: TS broadcast throws when not in a team context or when the team file cannot be read.
TS recipients are all teamFile.members except the sender by case-insensitive name.
TS no-recipient and success outputs use success/message/recipients/routing with message 'Message broadcast to N teammate(s): ...'.
writeToMailbox catches/logs write failures instead of surfacing per-recipient failed output.

go_evidence.note: Go broadcast recipient selection skips members with IsActive == false and deduplicates names.
Go mailbox broadcast records delivered and failed lists, sets success based on failed count, and returns 'Message broadcast to delivered/total teammate(s)'.
When no team config is loaded, Go broadcasts over MessageBus and returns an Envelope.
Current alignment tests expect the Go MessageBus envelope/broadcast quorum behavior, not the current TS SendMessageTool output.

gaps.impact: The same broadcast request can target a different recipient set, succeed/fail under different conditions, and return a different output shape. Go's partial-success bookkeeping may be useful, but it is not TS parity.

gaps.title: Structured control message payloads and lifecycle side effects are incomplete or over-broad
gaps.description: TS SendMessage accepts only shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response structured inputs. Its plan approval response includes inherited permissionMode, plan rejection writes default feedback when none is supplied, shutdown approval includes pane/backend metadata when known, and non-in-process approval schedules gracefulShutdown. Go accepts extra structured message types on its no-team MessageBus path, misses permissionMode/default feedback in mailbox payloads, omits paneId/backendType from shutdown approval payloads, and marks members inactive/aborts local background sessions instead of matching TS graceful process-exit behavior.

ts_evidence.note: TS structured input union is limited to shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response.
TS validates shutdown_response target and rejection reason.
TS plan approval requires isTeamLead and includes permissionMode inherited from the leader mode.
TS plan rejection writes feedback into the mailbox payload.
TS defaults missing rejection feedback to 'Plan needs revision' before calling handlePlanRejection.
TS shutdown approval looks up own pane/backend type, aborts in-process tasks, or schedules gracefulShutdown for other backends.
ShutdownApprovedMessage schema includes optional paneId and backendType.

go_evidence.note: Go decodes any map/object into structuredSendMessage and relies on later switch handling.
No-team structured path accepts plan_approval_request, shutdown_ack, and ask_user_question in addition to TS SendMessage input types.
Go shutdown approval/rejection payloads omit paneId/backendType; approval marks inactive and calls Background.AbortAgent when available.
Go plan approval response payload omits permissionMode, and rejection only writes feedback when the input feedback is non-empty.
Existing tests cover shutdown request/target/inactive state but not permissionMode, default feedback, pane/backend metadata, or graceful process exit.

gaps.impact: Workers may not inherit permission mode after plan approval, rejected plans can receive a payload without the TS default feedback, leader shutdown handling lacks backend metadata, and Go accepts or routes structured types the current TS SendMessage schema would reject.

gaps.title: Permission/read-only handling and supported error semantics do not match TS
gaps.description: For the supported non-bridge subset, TS marks plain string SendMessage calls read-only and structured messages non-read-only. Go classifies all SendMessage calls as medium risk through the generic permission system. For bridge, which is excluded from this report's candidate scope, Go currently implements only an Execute-time grant registry and tests that a granted bridge target falls through to no-transport behavior; this is not equivalent to TS checkPermissions if bridge is ever reintroduced.

ts_evidence.note: TS isReadOnly returns true exactly when input.message is a string.
TS checkPermissions allows normal targets and asks with classifierApprovable:false for bridge targets.

TS validateInput returns specific validation messages/errorCode 9 for empty to, empty address target, qualified names, summary, broadcast, cross-session structured messages, and shutdown_response constraints.

go_evidence.note: Go ClassifyRisk returns RiskMedium for SendMessage without inspecting whether the message is plain text or structured.
Current tests assert allow-all mode bypasses prompting for SendMessage but do not model TS isReadOnly semantics.
Go validates several TS-like constraints but returns Go ToolResult errors rather than TS validateInput errorCode results.
Go bridge consent is enforced inside Execute via bridgePermissionGranted instead of a pre-execution permission decision.
Bridge tests confirm there is no transport; after grant the call merely avoids the gate refusal.

gaps.impact: Plain messages may be over-permissioned, structured messages are not distinguished in risk/read-only metadata, and validation/permission behavior is not shaped like TS. The bridge note should stay out of delivery parity unless the repo decides to re-enable that path.

gaps.title: Go alignment tests partly encode stale/nonexistent TS contracts and miss current TS parity cases
gaps.description: Several SendMessage alignment tests reference TS files that are not present in the current ../src/tools/SendMessageTool directory and assert an envelope/InflightTable contract that the current TS SendMessageTool.ts does not expose. At the same time, tests do not cover sender spoofing rejection, TS mailbox layout/read flags/colors, current TS direct/broadcast output shapes, plan approval permissionMode/default feedback, or TS isReadOnly behavior. Targeted Go verification is currently also blocked by an unrelated provider build error.

ts_evidence.note: Current TS output union is success/message/routing, broadcast recipients, request_id/target, or request_id response; there is no Envelope type in this directory.
Current TS maps tool results to jsonStringify(data) from that output union.
Current SendMessage implementation is buildTool around the output union in this file; it does not import or expose Envelope/InflightTable/SendAndAwait-style result machinery.

go_evidence.note: Comments say the tests pin an envelope/InflightTable target contract and are expected to fail until that machinery is wired in.
Tests assert top-level request_id/kind/reply_to/delivered/recipients for direct sends, which is the Go Envelope shape.
Tests accept plan_approval_request, shutdown_ack, and ask_user_question as SendMessage structured inputs even though the current TS SendMessage schema does not.
Current tests cover direct mailbox, shutdown request/approval, and UDS, but not TS color/read/layout/permissionMode/default-feedback parity.
Targeted test run cannot currently build tools/permissions because classifyResponsesAPIError is undefined.

gaps.impact: Future implementation work may chase stale alignment targets and miss current TS regressions. A reliable red/green suite for this tool needs to be rebuilt against the actual current TS baseline before claiming full parity.

candidate_tasks.title: Remove or ignore Go-only SendMessage from/content inputs for user-facing calls
acceptance: User-facing SendMessage derives sender from runtime/team/env context only; input from cannot spoof team-lead or another teammate.
TS-compatible calls require message for user-facing SendMessage; content is either removed, ignored, or moved behind an internal-only compatibility path with explicit tests.
Pending-reply drain behavior no longer depends on caller-supplied from in the TS-compatible SendMessage path.
Regression tests show from=team-lead cannot authorize plan_approval_response unless runtime context is actually team lead.

candidate_tasks.title: Align SendMessage schema, description, availability, and read-only metadata with TS
acceptance: Published Name and Description match TS: SendMessage / 'Send a message to another agent'.
Published schema documents teammate, '*', and supported UDS targets; structured message objects are constrained to TS SendMessage's three structured types.
SendMessage visibility follows TS isAgentSwarmsEnabled-equivalent gating in normal tool assembly, while preserving any intentional coordinator/simple-mode exception with explicit tests.
Plain string messages are represented as read-only in the Go permission/risk layer; structured messages are not.
Unsupported bridge delivery remains explicitly out of scope unless a separate bridge transport parity task is created.

candidate_tasks.title: Replace or isolate the Go-only MessageBus fallback from the TS-compatible SendMessage path
acceptance: TS-compatible direct SendMessage without an active team config follows TS mailbox/default-team behavior or returns the same validation/error semantics TS would expose; it does not silently switch to Envelope output.
If MessageBus send/await remains needed for Go internals, it is moved behind a clearly internal transport or separate tool path and no longer changes the public SendMessage contract.
Direct SendMessage output in the public path is {success,message,routing?}, not Envelope.
Tests distinguish TS-compatible SendMessage from any internal MessageBus transport.

candidate_tasks.title: Align mailbox persistence, read lifecycle, and routing color metadata
acceptance: Mailbox write/read format is compatible with TS TeammateMessage, including read:false on write and optional color/summary fields.
Inbox path/layout is TS-compatible or a tested compatibility adapter reads/writes both Go and TS layouts without losing messages.
Mailbox read lifecycle preserves read/audit semantics equivalent to TS markMessagesAsRead; destructive read/remove behavior is not used for the TS-compatible path unless explicitly isolated.
Direct SendMessage routing includes senderColor and targetColor when available from team state/config.
Tests assert file layout, read flag behavior, color round-trip, and direct routing color fields.

candidate_tasks.title: Align broadcast validation, recipients, failure semantics, and output
acceptance: Broadcast without active team context returns the TS-style 'Not in a team context...' failure instead of MessageBus envelope output.
Broadcast to a missing team returns the TS-style Team does not exist failure.
Recipient selection matches TS: every team file member except sender by case-insensitive name; no extra IsActive filter in the TS-compatible path.
Successful broadcast output matches TS success/message/recipients/routing shape and message wording.
If Go keeps partial-success bookkeeping, it is isolated from the TS-compatible output path or documented as non-parity internal behavior with tests.

candidate_tasks.title: Align structured SendMessage control payloads and shutdown/plan lifecycle effects
acceptance: Structured SendMessage user-facing input accepts only shutdown_request, shutdown_response, and plan_approval_response, matching TS.
Plan approval is authorized from real team-lead runtime state, not input from.
Approved plan payload includes permissionMode with TS plan-mode default handling.
Rejected plan payload includes feedback, defaulting to 'Plan needs revision' when omitted.
Shutdown approval payload includes paneId/backendType when known.
Approved shutdown lifecycle matches TS for in-process and non-in-process equivalents, including actual session/process termination semantics or a documented Go-equivalent with tests.

candidate_tasks.title: Refresh SendMessage parity tests against the current TS baseline
acceptance: Alignment tests reference only files and behavior present in the current TS baseline: ../src/tools.ts, ../src/tools/SendMessageTool/SendMessageTool.ts, prompt.ts, constants.ts, teammateMailbox.ts, peerAddress.ts, LocalAgentTask, and resumeAgent.
Tests stop asserting nonexistent Envelope.ts/types.ts/structured.ts/leader_inbox.ts/SendAndAwait.ts contracts as TS SendMessage parity.

New red/green tests cover sender spoofing, strict input surface, no-team direct message behavior, direct output/routing colors, mailbox read flags/layout, broadcast output, plan approval permissionMode/default feedback, shutdown pane/backend metadata, and plain-message read-only classification.
Test package build blockers unrelated to SendMessage are either resolved upstream or documented so SendMessage verification can run deterministically.
